memo:
### Position read
The opponent opened Red from (0,3) to (3,3). We moved Blue from (4,7) to the safe center square (4,4). Red still controls (3,3); the other two center squares are empty before Yellow's reply.

### Our plan
On Green's turn, take (4,3) from (4,0) if it remains open. Longer term, place a Blue anchor at (2,3); after our Green vacates (4,3), Blue can move from (4,4) to (4,3) and sandwich Red at (3,3) against that anchor. Keep at least one center square occupied to prevent an opponent center win.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent immediately prioritized central occupation with Red. Expect Yellow to block (4,3) or occupy (3,4).

### Lessons
Avoid Blue at (3,4) while Red remains at (3,3): Red can later land at (3,5) and sandwich it. Central pieces are safest where the opponent lacks an existing same-color far flank.

### Position read
The opponent holds center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; we hold (4,4) with Blue. Green moved from (5,0) to (5,5), blocking Yellow’s route from (7,5) to (4,5), which otherwise could sandwich Blue at (4,4) against Yellow at (4,3).

### Our plan
If the position permits, develop Blue from (2,7) to (2,3) as a safe central anchor while retaining Blue at (4,4). Seek a later sandwich of Red at (3,3), especially if Yellow vacates (4,3). Keep occupying or contesting at least one center square.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is aggressively filling central squares and used Yellow to obstruct our intended Green entry at (4,3). Expect attempts to dislodge Blue at (4,4) or claim (3,4).

### Lessons
Always scan for a landing square that sandwiches a center piece against an opponent’s existing center piece. Blocking an attacker’s travel lane can preserve the center while another color develops.

### Position read
Blue moved from (2,7) to (2,4), sandwiching and capturing Red at (3,4) against Blue at (4,4). Red now has 1 loss. The opponent still occupies center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; we occupy (4,4), while (3,4) is now empty. Green at (5,5) continues blocking Yellow’s direct route into (4,5).

### Our plan
Preserve Blue at (4,4) to deny center victory. On Green’s next turn, look for entry to (3,4) or another move that strengthens control without enabling a sandwich. Blue at (2,4) can potentially descend into (3,4) if still empty, giving us three-point central pressure and possible enclosure threats.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is aggressively building in the center and may now use Yellow to occupy (3,4), attack Blue at (4,4), or reconnect the central formation. Expect Red to replace its captured center piece later.

### Lessons
When opposing pieces line up between two same-colored pieces, prioritize the immediate sandwich: it both inflicts a loss and dismantles center occupation. Continue checking every central landing for friendly-fire lines and counter-sandwiches.

### Position read
We moved from (5,5) to (4,5), blocking the opponent’s immediate (4,6)->(4,5) sandwich against our piece at (4,4). The opponent holds center squares (3,3) and (4,3); we hold (4,4), and (3,4) remains empty. Losses: opponent’s top-edge color 1; all others 0.

### Our plan
Preserve (4,4) as the center-victory blocker. On our next turn, consider moving the piece at (2,4) to (3,4), provided this neither enables a tactical capture nor creates dangerous friendly fire. Our piece at (4,5) should continue restricting the opponent at (4,6) and support central control.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is concentrating pieces around the center and just positioned at (4,6) for a sandwich threat. Expect attempts to dislodge (4,4), occupy (3,4), or attack the new blocker at (4,5).

### Lessons
Check one-move sandwiches before pursuing center occupation. The key current alignment is opponent (4,3), our piece (4,4), and the contested landing square (4,5).

### Position read
We moved Blue from (2,4) to (3,4). We now occupy center squares (3,4) and (4,4), while the opponent occupies (3,3) and (4,3). Our Green at (4,5) still blocks the Yellow at (4,6). Losses remain: opponent’s top-edge color 1; all others 0.

### Our plan
Hold both right-hand center squares and watch for captures that can dislodge either piece. Use the Green turn to reinforce the center or constrain the opponent’s pieces at (3,3), (4,3), and (4,6). Avoid the tempting Blue move to (4,7), which would capture both the opponent at (4,6) and our Green at (4,5).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is concentrating around the center and may try to build same-color sandwich endpoints against our central pair. Expect the next move to pressure (3,4), (4,4), or reposition the piece at (4,6).

### Lessons
Mixed opponent colors cannot form sandwich endpoints together. Before every move, inspect all four landing-square rays for friendly fire as well as hostile captures.

### Position read
We moved our left-edge piece from (2,0) to (2,3). We still hold the right-hand center squares (3,4) and (4,4); the opponent holds (3,3) and (4,3). Our piece at (2,3) blocks the upward route from (3,3), whose other adjacent squares are occupied. Our advanced piece remains at (4,5), beside the opponent at (4,6). Losses: opponent’s top-edge color 1; all others 0. The opponent’s bottom-edge color has one consecutive pass pending.

### Our plan
Maintain both right-hand center squares while tightening around the opponent’s central pair. Look for a safe same-color sandwich or enclosure, but preserve our piece at (4,5): moving it to (3,5) would allow an opponent move from (0,6) to (3,6) to sandwich it together with our center piece at (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is centralizing but just passed with the bottom-edge color. Expect the top-edge color to relieve the congested piece at (3,3), attack our central pair, or exploit mixed-color sandwich lines.

### Lessons
Check whether every development square becomes the middle of an opponent sandwich. Mixed colors may be captured in one line, including teammates; only the two endpoints must match the mover.

### Position read
We moved from (4,4) to (3,4), retaining one center square and breaking the threat from (4,6) moving to (4,7), which otherwise would have sandwiched our pieces at (4,5) and (4,4). Our new piece at (3,4) sits safely between opponent pieces at (3,3) and (3,5); static or self-entered sandwiches do not capture. The opponent holds (3,3) and (4,3). Losses: opponent’s top-edge color 1, our right-edge color 1, others 0. The opponent’s bottom-edge color has one pending pass.

### Our plan
Keep (3,4) occupied and use our next turn to contest (4,3)/(4,4) or tighten the central enclosure. Watch for either row-3 opponent endpoint moving away and later returning, which could trigger a capture of (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent attacks mixed-color lines and recently used a same-color row-3 flank to take our former center piece. Their bottom-edge color previously passed despite having moves.

### Lessons
Moving into an existing sandwich is safe. Before preserving a flank, check whether an opponent can extend beyond a mixed line and capture both of our colors.

### Position read
We hold (3,4); the opponent holds the other three center squares. Our piece at (2,3) is the upper endpoint of a new column-3 tactic, with our moved piece now at (6,3). Losses: opponent colors 1 and 0; our colors 1 and 1. No eliminations.

### Our plan
Threaten (6,3)->(5,3), sandwiching the opponent pieces at (4,3) and (3,3) against (2,3). The piece at (3,3) is currently immobile. If the opponent vacates (4,3) sideways, consider (6,3)->(4,3), which occupies a center and captures (3,3). If they retreat from (4,3) to (5,3), keep the endpoints intact and deny an easy return to center. Continue protecting (3,4), since vacating it could allow immediate opponent center occupation.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes mixed-color sandwiches and center pressure. Their bottom-edge color has previously passed once but is now active.

### Lessons
Column endpoints can force a center defender to move even when the capture is one turn away. Recheck self-entered sandwiches: they remain safe until an endpoint later lands and triggers capture.

### Position read
Our Blue move (3,7)->(3,6) sandwiches the opponent piece at (3,5) against our Blue at (3,4), raising that opponent color to 2 losses. We retain (3,4); the opponent still holds (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4). Our Green endpoints remain at (2,3) and (6,3). Our losses are 1 and 1; opponent losses are now 2 and 0.

### Our plan
On the next Green turn, if (5,3) stays empty, play (6,3)->(5,3) to capture the pieces at (4,3) and (3,3), eliminating the opponent color already on 2 losses. If (4,3) moves sideways while (5,3) remains clear, play (6,3)->(4,3) to occupy center and capture (3,3). If the opponent blocks at (5,3), preserve the endpoints and seek a way to dislodge that blocker. Keep our Blue at (3,4) secure to prevent center occupation.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent favors center pressure but must now address the column-3 capture threat or risk an elimination.

### Lessons
A safe material capture is strongest when it raises a color to the elimination threshold immediately before a separate forced sandwich.

### Position read
We played (6,3)->(5,3), sandwiching the opponent pieces at (4,3) and (3,3) against our piece at (2,3). This should raise the opponent losses to 3 and 1, eliminating the color previously on 2 losses; its surviving pieces at (0,1), (0,5), and (3,2) become Void. Our losses remain 1 and 1. Center occupancy after capture: ours at (3,4); opponent at (4,4); (3,3) and (4,3) empty.

### Our plan
Exploit the eliminated color’s inability to capture while contesting the center. Preserve (3,4), and seek occupation of (3,3) and (4,3) with our pieces. Watch for sandwiches involving our Green pieces at (2,3) and (5,3), especially if the opponent places pieces between them.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent continued a harmless bottom-row move instead of answering the forced column-3 sandwich, allowing the elimination tactic.

### Lessons
When a forced multi-piece sandwich is available, execute it immediately if it crosses an elimination threshold; Void remnants then lose all capturing power.

### Position read
We played (5,7)->(5,4), sandwiching the opponent piece at (4,4) against our piece at (3,4). The opponent’s active color should now have 2 losses, while the already eliminated color has Void pieces at (0,1), (0,5), and (3,3). Our losses remain 1 and 1. Center: opponent Void at (3,3), ours at (3,4), with (4,3) and (4,4) empty after capture.

### Our plan
On our next Green turn, consider (5,3)->(4,3) to claim a third center square if safe. We would then need (4,4) for immediate center victory, while also seeking one more capture to eliminate the opponent color on 2 losses. Preserve the Blue anchors at (3,4) and (5,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent’s eliminated color used a Void move to reoccupy (3,3), contesting the center but posing no capture threat. The other color may now try to re-enter (4,4) or disrupt our center formation.

### Lessons
Use aligned same-color anchors to harvest center occupants. Void pieces still count for center control and blocking, but their moves cannot capture.

### Position read
We played (5,3)->(4,3), sandwiching and removing the opponent Void at (3,3) against our Green at (2,3). We now occupy center squares (3,4) with Blue and (4,3) with Green; Yellow occupies (4,4), while (3,3) is empty. The active opponent color remains one loss from elimination. Our losses remain 1 and 1.

### Our plan
Protect the center pair at (3,4) and (4,3). Seek a Blue or Green alignment that captures Yellow at (4,4), immediately eliminating that color and converting its survivors to Void. If Yellow vacates, aim to occupy (4,4) and then (3,3) without unnecessarily exchanging one center square for another.

### Opponent tendencies
The eliminated color uses Void moves to contest central squares. The surviving color re-entered (4,4) after losing a piece, prioritizing disruption of our center victory.

### Lessons
A move onto (4,3) both gains a center square and triggers the vertical Green sandwich through (3,3). Capturing central Void pieces matters because they count toward center victory despite being harmless offensively.

### Position read
Blue moved (5,4)->(6,4), retaining Blue at (3,4) and Green at (4,3). Yellow on (4,4) is trapped tactically: staying permits Blue (6,4)->(5,4) to sandwich it against (3,4); moving down to (5,4) permits Blue (3,4)->(4,4) to sandwich it against (6,4). Its only escape is sideways.

### Our plan
On Green's turn, play (2,3)->(3,3) unless the position unexpectedly offers an immediate win. Then: if Yellow stayed on (4,4), capture via Blue (6,4)->(5,4); if it moved to (5,4), capture via Blue (3,4)->(4,4). Either capture is Yellow's third loss and eliminates the opponent team. If Yellow fled sideways, play Blue (6,4)->(4,4) after Green occupies (3,3), completing all four center squares.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central disruption, but the current geometry gives no safe central defense.

### Lessons
Retreating a sandwich flank can create a forced re-entry capture while also preserving a center-winning route.

### Position read
We now hold (3,3), (3,4), and (4,3); only (4,4) remains for a center win. Yellow escaped the prior trap by moving (4,4)->(5,4) and captured our Blue flank at (6,4), so the planned sandwich no longer works. Yellow has two losses; Red is already eliminated and has one Void piece at (0,5) plus another at (3,1).

### Our plan
Prioritize the center win. Seek a move by a noncentral piece into (4,4), preserving the other three occupied centers. Blue can develop toward row 4 or column 4; Green can consider (4,3)->(4,4) only if (4,3) can be refilled safely. Watch for immediate captures that give Yellow its third loss.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent recognized the forced-capture geometry and escaped by capturing the supporting Blue piece. Expect Void Red moves and Yellow moves to target or occupy the remaining center square and obstruct refill routes.

### Lessons
Recalculate after every capture: losing a stationary sandwich flank can invalidate both the elimination tactic and an apparent center-completion route.

### Position read
We occupy (3,3), (4,3), and now (4,4); (3,4) is temporarily vacant. Blue at (3,6) has a clear route through (3,5) to refill (3,4). Yellow has two losses and its nearest piece at (5,4) cannot enter (3,4) because our Blue at (4,4) blocks the file. Red is eliminated; its Void pieces cannot capture.

### Our plan
Keep all three occupied centers fixed through the intervening Yellow, Green, and Void Red turns. On the next Blue turn, play (3,6)->(3,4) for immediate center victory if the route and central pieces remain intact. Green should make a quiet move that does not vacate (3,3) or (4,3).

### Opponent tendencies
Expect Yellow to attack or dislodge a central piece rather than contest (3,4) directly. Void Red may try to block (3,5) or otherwise obstruct the Blue refill route, though it cannot capture.

### Lessons
A two-step center relay is viable when the vacated center cannot be reached by the opponent before the refill and the replacement piece already has a clear rook line.

### Position read
We retain three center squares: (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4). The opponent’s last normal color has two losses, with a vulnerable piece at (5,4). Our pieces at (3,6) and (6,7) create two immediate winning routes.

### Our plan
After the opponent’s Void turn, win with whichever route remains open: move (3,6)->(3,4) to complete center occupation, or move (6,7)->(6,4) to sandwich the piece at (5,4) against our piece at (4,4), causing the opponent’s second-color elimination. The Void at (4,5) can block one route via (3,5) or (6,5), but not both.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has actively contested the center. Their Void pieces cannot capture, so the only defense is line obstruction.

### Lessons
When center completion and a third-loss capture use separate lanes, preserve both threats; a single intervening move cannot answer the fork.

### Position read
Blue’s move (6,7)->(6,4) captures Yellow at (5,4) against Blue at (4,4). Yellow reaches three losses and is eliminated; the opponent’s other color was already eliminated.

### Our plan
The game is won immediately by team elimination.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent blocked the center-completion lane with a Void piece but could not cover the independent elimination threat.

### Lessons
A fork between center occupation and third-loss capture is decisive when the defensive move can obstruct only one lane.
